procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Routine f/u, first visit since the vulvar cancer diagnosis. Radical local excision 12/5, stage IA, margins clear, no further treatment needed per gyn-onc. Healed, post-op check fine. Still using clobetasol on the lichen sclerosus. Says she feels lucky it was caught small. Back teaching since the new year.
DM: no lows, metformin BID. HTN: no complaints. Reflux quiet on omeprazole.
Meds: lisinopril 20, HCTZ 12.5, metformin 1000 BID, omeprazole 20, clobetasol oint prn. NKDA.
O: BP at goal. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. No edema.
A/P
1. Vulvar SCC stage IA s/p excision — gyn-onc surveillance q6 months, next in April.
2. T2DM — A1c today.
3. HTN/ADPKD — BMP today.
4. GERD/hiatal hernia — continue omeprazole.
Mammogram in March. RTC late spring.

reports.text: Bilateral CC and MLO views with tomosynthesis, compared with 3/2023. Scattered fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, calcification or distortion. Stable appearance.

documents.title: Gynecologic Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
GYN ONCOLOGY SURVEILLANCE VISIT
Date: 04/18/2024
Valerie Slattery, 54. Stage IA keratinizing SCC of the left labium majus, radical local excision 12/2023, margins negative.
Interval: no new itching, sores or bleeding. Uses clobetasol twice weekly as maintenance.
Meds: lisinopril, HCTZ, metformin, omeprazole, clobetasol. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: excision scar well healed, no nodularity. Lichen sclerosus changes stable, no new plaques or ulcers. No inguinal adenopathy. Speculum and bimanual normal.
Impression: no evidence of disease.
Plan: continue clobetasol maintenance. Return in 6 months.
Gynecologic Oncology

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

reports.text: Extra-axial, well-circumscribed, dural-based mass in the right frontal region with partial calcification. No acute hemorrhage. No hydrocephalus. Ventricles otherwise normal. Calvarium intact.
reports.conclusion: Right frontal extra-axial dural-based mass with partial calcification, most consistent with meningioma. MRI recommended.

reports.study: MRI brain with and without contrast
reports.text: Right frontal extra-axial lesion with broad dural base and homogeneous enhancement after contrast, with a dural tail. No other lesions. No acute infarct. No hydrocephalus.
reports.conclusion: Homogeneously enhancing right frontal dural-based lesion with dural tail, consistent with meningioma.

documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD — regional hospital
Arrival 05/02/2024 07:55. Received by fax.

CC: headaches, seizures.
HPI: 54F. For about six months a constant dull ache over the right forehead, worst on waking. Recently has had seizures, and now occasional blurry vision. Brought in today after another episode at home.
PMH: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, ADPKD, DVT 2021, GERD/hiatal hernia, vulvar lichen sclerosus and stage IA vulvar SCC excised 12/2023.
Meds: lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, omeprazole 20 mg, clobetasol ointment.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: teacher, former smoker, occasional wine.

Exam: awake, alert, oriented. Mild weakness of the left upper extremity; otherwise strength intact. Fundi without papilledema. Speech normal. No neck stiffness.
Labs: basic chemistry and CBC unremarkable.
CT head without contrast: right frontal extra-axial, well-circumscribed dural-based mass with partial calcification.
MRI brain with contrast: homogeneously enhancing lesion with a dural tail.

MDM: new right frontal meningioma causing headache, seizures and mild left arm weakness. Levetiracetam loaded and continued at 500 mg BID. Dexamethasone started. Neurosurgery consulted and accepts for admission.
Disposition: admitted to neurosurgery.
Emergency Medicine

medications.sig: Taper as directed: 4 mg twice daily for 3 days, then 2 mg twice daily for 3 days, then 2 mg daily for 3 days, then stop

reports.text: Specimen: dura-based mass, right frontal, resection. Meningothelial meningioma with whorls and psammoma bodies. No brain invasion. Mitotic count low. No atypical features.

documents.title: Neurosurgery Discharge Summary
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY — Neurosurgery, regional hospital
Admitted 05/02/2024   Discharged 05/09/2024

Diagnosis: right frontal meningioma presenting with headache, seizures and mild left arm weakness.
Procedure: right frontotemporal craniotomy and resection of meningioma, 05/06/2024.

Course: admitted from the ED on levetiracetam and dexamethasone. Seizure-free throughout the stay. Underwent uncomplicated craniotomy with gross total resection on 05/06. Post-op CT without hemorrhage. Left arm weakness improving by discharge. Headache much improved.
Pathology: meningothelial meningioma, WHO grade 1.

Discharge medications:
- levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily (new)
- dexamethasone taper over 9 days (new)
- lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily, clobetasol ointment as needed (unchanged)
Allergies: NKDA.

Instructions: no driving for 6 months from the last seizure, per state law. Keep the incision dry for 5 days, staples out at 10-14 days. Call for fever, wound drainage, new weakness or seizure.
Follow-up: neurosurgery clinic in 5 weeks; MRI at 6 months. PCP within 1-2 weeks.
Neurosurgery

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-hospital visit. Partner drove her.
Admitted 5/2-5/9 after the ED found a right frontal meningioma (months of morning headaches, then seizures, mild L arm weakness). Craniotomy 5/6, gross total resection, WHO grade 1. Discharge summary reviewed.
Since home: no seizures. Headache mild and improving. Left hand grip feels almost normal. Finishing the dexamethasone taper this week. Staples out at neurosurgery yesterday.
Med rec: levetiracetam 500 BID (new), dexamethasone taper (ends this week), lisinopril 20, HCTZ 12.5, metformin 1000 BID, omeprazole 20, clobetasol prn. NKDA.
Exam: incision healing well, no erythema or drainage. Alert, fluent. Strength 5/5 bilaterally except slight L grip weakness. Gait normal. Heart RRR, lungs clear.
A/P
1. Meningioma s/p resection — recovering well. Neurosurgery f/u in June, MRI at 6 months.
2. Seizures — on levetiracetam, none since surgery. Reviewed no driving for 6 months; partner and a colleague are covering rides. School note for medical leave through end of the school year.
3. T2DM — continue metformin; BMP today.
4. HTN — at goal.
Call with any seizure, mood change on levetiracetam, or new headache.

documents.title: Neurosurgery Follow-up
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
NEUROSURGERY CLINIC NOTE
Date: 06/13/2024
Valerie Slattery, 54, five weeks after right frontotemporal craniotomy for a WHO grade 1 meningioma.
She reports no seizures since surgery and only an occasional mild headache. The left arm feels normal to her.
Medications: levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily, lisinopril, HCTZ, metformin, omeprazole, clobetasol. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: incision fully healed. Cranial nerves intact. Strength 5/5 in all extremities including the left arm. Gait normal.
Plan: continue levetiracetam until the 6-month visit; MRI brain with and without contrast before that visit. Driving restriction continues until 6 months seizure-free. May return to teaching in the fall.
Neurosurgery

documents.title: Keppra refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body:
Hi, I'm down to a week of the levetiracetam and the neurosurgery office said to ask you for refills until my October visit. Also is it okay to keep taking the omeprazole long term? I read something online.
Thanks, Valerie

documents.title: RE: Keppra refill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sent 90 days of levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily to your pharmacy. On the omeprazole: with a hiatal hernia and symptoms that come back without it, staying on the lowest dose that works is reasonable. We can talk about trying every other day at your physical in September if you'd like.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical. Back in the classroom last week, a little tired at the end of the day but managing.
Year in review: right frontal meningioma resected 5/2024 (WHO 1), seizure-free on levetiracetam, MRI and neurosurgery visit in October. Vulvar SCC stage IA excised 12/2023, NED at April surveillance. Reflux controlled.
Eye exam with optometry this August, no retinopathy per pt; asked her to have the report sent.
Mood good. PHQ-9 3.

Meds: levetiracetam 500 BID, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 12.5, metformin 1000 BID, omeprazole 20, clobetasol prn. NKDA.
Exam: BP at goal. Well healed right frontotemporal scar. Neuro nonfocal. Heart RRR, lungs clear, abdomen soft. No edema. Feet normal sensation and pulses.

A/P
- Preventive: flu and COVID in October. Mammogram March. Colonoscopy 2030. Shingrix and Tdap complete.
- T2DM: A1c, urine microalbumin today.
- HTN/ADPKD: CMP.
- Meningioma s/p resection, seizures: per neurosurgery.
- Vulvar SCC: gyn-onc in October.
Offered a trial of omeprazole every other day; she prefers to stay on daily dosing.
RTC 4 months.

GYN ONCOLOGY SURVEILLANCE VISIT
Date: 10/17/2024
Ms. Slattery returns ten months after excision of a stage IA left vulvar SCC. Since we last saw her she had a right frontal meningioma resected (5/2024) and is recovering well.
No vulvar symptoms beyond occasional itch controlled with clobetasol twice weekly.
Meds: levetiracetam, lisinopril, HCTZ, metformin, omeprazole, clobetasol. Allergies: NKDA.

events.reason: Shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain

conditions.label: Pulmonary embolism
conditions.note: acute bilateral lower lobe segmental emboli after long-haul flight

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (10 mg) by mouth twice daily for 7 days, then 1 tablet (5 mg) twice daily

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia. Normal axis and intervals. No ST-segment or T-wave changes.

CT angiography of the chest, pulmonary embolism protocol. Filling defects in segmental pulmonary arteries of the right and left lower lobes. Main and lobar arteries patent. RV to LV ratio normal; no septal bowing. Lungs clear without infarct or effusion. Known sliding hiatal hernia.
reports.conclusion: Acute bilateral lower lobe segmental pulmonary emboli. No CT evidence of right heart strain.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD — regional hospital
Date of visit: 11/08/2024

Chief complaint: short of breath, chest pain with breathing.
HPI: 54-year-old woman, abrupt shortness of breath and sharp chest pain on inspiration beginning about two hours before arrival. Got home two days ago from a long-haul flight from Asia. Prior DVT three years ago. Meningioma resected in May; stage IA vulvar SCC excised last December.
Medications: lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg BID, omeprazole 20 mg daily, clobetasol ointment; recently finished a levetiracetam taper.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Triage vitals: BP 135/85, HR 110, RR 22, SpO2 94% on room air.
Exam: anxious, speaking in short sentences. Lungs clear. Heart tachycardic, regular. Legs without swelling or calf tenderness.

Results: D-dimer elevated. High-sensitivity troponin normal. BNP normal. ABG on room air shows hypoxemia with a normal A-a gradient. ECG: sinus tachycardia, no ST changes.
Modified Wells score 4.5: PE likely.
CTA chest: acute segmental emboli in both lower lobes, no right heart strain.

Assessment: acute pulmonary embolism after prolonged air travel in a patient with prior DVT. Hemodynamically stable.
Plan: apixaban 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily; first dose given here. Neurosurgery note reviewed, now six months post-op without bleeding concerns. Observation overnight for oxygen and heart rate.
Emergency Medicine

documents.title: Observation Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
OBSERVATION DISCHARGE SUMMARY — regional hospital
Admitted 11/08/2024 (observation)   Discharged 11/09/2024
Diagnosis: acute bilateral segmental pulmonary emboli, travel-associated, history of DVT 2021.
Course: placed in observation on apixaban. Heart rate settled overnight and saturations stayed above 94% on room air; no supplemental oxygen needed by morning. Ambulated without desaturation. No bleeding.
Discharge medications: apixaban 10 mg BID through 11/14, then 5 mg BID (new; 30-day free trial card given). Continue lisinopril 20 mg, HCTZ 12.5 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, omeprazole 20 mg, clobetasol ointment as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Duration of anticoagulation to be decided by PCP; at least 3-6 months.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week.
Hospital Medicine

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after ED/observation stay 11/8-11/9 for bilateral segmental PE, two days after flying home from Asia. Prior DVT 2021.
Today: breathing almost back to normal, winded on the stairs at school. Pleuritic pain gone. No bleeding or bruising on apixaban. Finishing the 10 mg BID loading dose today, 5 mg BID from tomorrow. Off levetiracetam since the taper ended last week, no seizures.
Meds: apixaban 10 mg BID x 7 days then 5 mg BID, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 12.5, metformin 1000 BID, omeprazole 20, clobetasol prn. NKDA.
Exam: comfortable, sats normal on RA, HR normal. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No calf swelling or tenderness.
A/P
PE, provoked by long-haul travel, second VTE. Discussed duration: plan about 6 months of apixaban, then reassess with her; she understands a second clot argues for at least that. Bleeding precautions, avoid NSAIDs. Check cost of apixaban after the free trial card runs out.
Future long flights: aisle seat, walk every hour, hydrate.
RTC February.

documents.title: Prior authorization — apixaban
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy notified us that her plan requires prior authorization for apixaban 5 mg BID after the trial supply. PA submitted with diagnosis of acute PE 11/8/2024 and planned 6-month course. Approved same day through 6/2025. Pharmacy and patient notified; copay $45/month.
